statement.p: A closed rectangular box with faces parallel to the coordinate planes has one bottom corner at the origin and the opposite top corner in the first octant on the plane 4 x + 2 y + z = 1. What is the maximum volume of such a box?

static.solution:
(x,y,z), the volume of the box is V=xyz. Since z=1 - 4 x - 2 y on the plane, the volume is given by V=xy (1 - 4 x - 2 y) = xy - 4 x^2 y - 2 xy^2. The domain is the triangular region 0\leq x\leq \frac{1}{4}, 0\leq y \leq (1 - 4 x)/2. At a critical point, \frac{\partial V}{\partial x} = y - 8 xy - 2 y^2 = y(1- x- 2 y) = 0, and \frac{\partial V}{\partial y} = x - 4 x^2 - 4 xy = x(1 - 4 x- 4 y) = 0. One solution is x=y=0. Another is x=0, y=\frac{1}{2}; another is y=0, x=\frac{1}{4}. Another is the solution of 1 - 8 x - 2 y = 0, \qquad 1 - 4 x - 4 y =0, namely x=\frac{1}{12}, y=\frac{1}{6}.
If either x=0 or y=0, then V=0, so these solutions do not give the maximum volume. Since D=V_{xx}V_{yy}-(V_{xy})^2 = (-8 y)(-4 x) - (1 - 8 x - 4 y)^2, at the remaining critical point we have D\left ( \frac{1}{12}, \frac{1}{6}\right ) = \left(-8 \cdot\frac1{6}\right) \left(-4\cdot\frac1{12}\right) - \left(1 - 8\cdot\frac1{12} - 4\cdot\frac1{6}\right)^2 = \frac{4}{9}-\frac{1}{9}=\frac{1}{3}>0, and V_{xx}(\frac1{12},\frac1{6})=-\frac{4}{3}\lt 0, the point x=\frac{1}{12},\, y=\frac{1}{6}, is a local maximum at which V= (1/12)(1/6) - 4(1/12)^2(1/6) - 2(1/12)(1/6)^2 = 1/216.
Since all points on the boundary of the domain give V=0, the local maximum is a global maximum.
